Why would anyone feel comfortable putting their life savings into an ecosystem where even the biggest players aren’t immune?

At some point, we need to acknowledge that this is doing serious damage to the industry’s reputation.

Mass adoption means nothing if we can’t earn people’s trust first.

My thoughts on the market and $BTC after the record breaking Binance hack 👇

$BTC has come down and filled this inefficiency, it tapped right at the Daily 200EMA & Top of the Bull market support band.

Up on a break of $80K, this was the top of my price range where I'd get interested again for long term value. I would expect BTC to hold its ground between here and $72K-$73K (which is close from here anyways).

If this was it, price recovers back above $80K and everything looks solid again, then that would be a sign of strength for me. These Daily 200EMA & Bull Market support band retests do pretty much always occur when a bear market transitions into a new bull market. They always look scary. This was the largest drawdown since the $58K-$87K rally. But still only -12% so nothing to go crazy over.

From my memory these post hack markets do tend to be somewhat choppy and take some time to recover usually. Especially because trust and sentiment take a big hit. That is a good recipe for a (local) bottom eventually, but it generally takes some time to play out.

We will see the occasional headlines on when the hacker is moving/selling BTC & ETH and might see some weakness on that news when it occurs. But the amounts are nothing the market would lose its sleep over at the current size of the market.

Low timeframe I am looking for a retest to the .786 fib level around ~$76.9K to see if that makes one of those marginally higher lows and then bounces. Those have been pretty reliable after big moves and retests for $BTC the past few years. If not, we patiently wait and see what happens.

This event was nowhere close to the damage something like the 10/10 market crash or whatever comparison some people are making. Different market environments as well so hard to compare these things.

Let the market and charts lead.

So to summarize: 
- Bitcoin at the top of the high timeframe value zone already. I like long term spot buys between here and $72K.
- Daily 200EMA & Bull Market support band retests are normal when transitioning in a new high timeframe uptrend.
- Hack not as bad or comparable as 10/10 imo
- Nothing changes for alts vs BTC specifically for me here. Some alts sold off more than others because of the hacked amount but have also retraced that already. Don't think there's any edge there specifically. Just need to remain selective as always.

$BTC has come down and filled this inefficiency, it tapped right at the Daily 200EMA & Top of the Bull market support band.

Up on a break of $80K, this was the top of my price range where I'd get interested again for long term value. I would expect BTC to hold its ground between here and $72K-$73K (which is close from here anyways).

If this was it, price recovers back above $80K and everything looks solid again, then that would be a sign of strength for me. These Daily 200EMA & Bull Market support band retests do pretty much always occur when a bear market transitions into a new bull market. They always look scary. This was the largest drawdown since the $58K-$87K rally. But still only -12% so nothing to go crazy over.

From my memory these post hack markets do tend to be somewhat choppy and take some time to recover usually. Especially because trust and sentiment take a big hit. That is a good recipe for a (local) bottom eventually, but it generally takes some time to play out.

We will see the occasional headlines on when the hacker is moving/selling BTC & ETH and might see some weakness on that news when it occurs. But the amounts are nothing the market would lose its sleep over at the current size of the market.

Low timeframe I am looking for a retest to the .786 fib level around ~$76.9K to see if that makes one of those marginally higher lows and then bounces. Those have been pretty reliable after big moves and retests for $BTC the past few years. If not, we patiently wait and see what happens.

This event was nowhere close to the damage something like the 10/10 market crash or whatever comparison some people are making. Different market environments as well so hard to compare these things.

Let the market and charts lead.

So to summarize: 
- Bitcoin at the top of the high timeframe value zone already. I like long term spot buys between here and $72K.
- Daily 200EMA & Bull Market support band retests are normal when transitioning in a new high timeframe uptrend.
- Hack not as bad or comparable as 10/10 imo
- Nothing changes for alts vs BTC specifically for me here. Some alts sold off more than others because of the hacked amount but have also retraced that already. Don't think there's any edge there specifically. Just need to remain selective as always.

It was a tough night, and I’m pretty tired. I was watching the hacker in real time and doing my best to keep all of you informed about what was happening.

The price is holding up relatively well, but I have to be honest: fear is back in the market. It’s still possible we move a bit lower from here, potentially toward my final target in the mid-$70s, which I’ve been talking about for weeks now.

That is also the final target of the accumulation strategy I shared with my X subscribers.

At the end of the day, my job is to manage risk and allocate capital to the best opportunities I can find. But it’s hard to ignore the bigger picture right now. There is war in different parts of the world, governments are increasingly talking about preparing for difficult scenarios, and almost every major asset class has been under pressure.

Stocks, crypto, gold, silver, currencies, nothing feels particularly safe right now. Inflation has also continued to eat away at the purchasing power of both the dollar and the euro.

The world simply feels very uncertain at the moment.

I also worry that political instability in the US could create even more stress for the markets, potentially leading to a much longer period of economic weakness. I obviously hope that never happens. I want to see the economy continue growing, especially with AI potentially driving another period of strong productivity and innovation over the coming years.

There are also plenty of countries and economies that are doing well, so I don’t want to make this sound like everything is doomed.

But we also have to acknowledge the other possibility: geopolitical conflicts, political decisions, or other major shocks could push the global economy into a much deeper downturn.

I don’t want to sound overly negative. I’m not a negative person.

But right now, the world feels uncertain, and I think it’s important to be prepared for different scenarios.

My thoughts on the market and $BTC after the record breaking Binance hack 👇

$BTC has come down and filled this inefficiency, it tapped right at the Daily 200EMA & Top of the Bull market support band.

Up on a break of $80K, this was the top of my price range where I'd get interested again for long term value. I would expect BTC to hold its ground between here and $72K-$73K (which is close from here anyways).

If this was it, price recovers back above $80K and everything looks solid again, then that would be a sign of strength for me. These Daily 200EMA & Bull Market support band retests do pretty much always occur when a bear market transitions into a new bull market. They always look scary. This was the largest drawdown since the $58K-$87K rally. But still only -12% so nothing to go crazy over.

From my memory these post hack markets do tend to be somewhat choppy and take some time to recover usually. Especially because trust and sentiment take a big hit. That is a good recipe for a (local) bottom eventually, but it generally takes some time to play out.

We will see the occasional headlines on when the hacker is moving/selling BTC & ETH and might see some weakness on that news when it occurs. But the amounts are nothing the market would lose its sleep over at the current size of the market.

Low timeframe I am looking for a retest to the .786 fib level around ~$76.9K to see if that makes one of those marginally higher lows and then bounces. Those have been pretty reliable after big moves and retests for $BTC the past few years. If not, we patiently wait and see what happens.

This event was nowhere close to the damage something like the 10/10 market crash or whatever comparison some people are making. Different market environments as well so hard to compare these things.

Let the market and charts lead.

So to summarize: 
- Bitcoin at the top of the high timeframe value zone already. I like long term spot buys between here and $72K.
- Daily 200EMA & Bull Market support band retests are normal when transitioning in a new high timeframe uptrend.
- Hack not as bad or comparable as 10/10 imo
- Nothing changes for alts vs BTC specifically for me here. Some alts sold off more than others because of the hacked amount but have also retraced that already. Don't think there's any edge there specifically. Just need to remain selective as always.
